title: Why Following Your Dreams Isn't Enough

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: The year was 1964.
The legendary singer Frank Sinatra met Mia Farrow, an up-and-coming actress, on a soundstage at 20th Century Fox.
sentences.zh: 传奇歌手弗兰克·辛纳屈在20世纪福克斯公司的摄影棚里遇到了初出茅庐的女演员米亚·法罗。

sentences.en: Despite their 30-year age difference, the two began dating and fell madly in love.
sentences.zh: 尽管两人有30岁的年龄差，他们还是开始约会并坠入了爱河。

sentences.en: Frank Sinatra bought Mia Farrow a massive 9-carat pear-shaped diamond ring.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克·辛纳屈给米亚·法罗买了一枚巨大的9克拉梨形钻戒。

sentences.en: He proposed at his home in Palm Springs.
sentences.zh: 他在棕榈泉的家中向她求婚。

sentences.en: The wedding itself was a small civil ceremony, but the celebration was lavish.
sentences.zh: 婚礼本身是一场小型民事仪式，但庆祝活动却极尽奢华。

sentences.en: The groom gifted its bride an expensive double-rowed diamond bracelet.
sentences.zh: 新郎送给新娘一条昂贵的双排钻石手链。

sentences.en: Not long after, Mia Farrow was on the set of Rosemary's Baby when she was issued divorce papers.
sentences.zh: 没过多久，米亚·法罗在拍摄《罗斯玛丽的婴儿》时收到了离婚协议书。

sentences.en: Frank Sinatra didn't want her to work.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克·辛纳屈不想让她工作。

sentences.en: He was just old-fashioned, Mia Farrow later explained.
sentences.zh: 米亚·法罗后来解释说，他只是思想守旧。

sentences.en: They divorced just two years after saying, I do.
sentences.zh: 他们在说出“我愿意”仅仅两年后就离婚了。

sentences.en: Did the couple not talk before they got married?
sentences.zh: 这对夫妇在结婚前没有交流过吗？

sentences.en: Did they not discuss their values?
sentences.zh: 他们没有讨论过彼此的价值观吗？

sentences.en: How is it they failed to see they were not on the same page on such an important question?
sentences.zh: 他们怎么会没发现自己在如此重要的问题上意见不合呢？

sentences.en: In 2014, two economics professors weighed in on the issue.
sentences.zh: 2014年，两位经济学教授对这个问题发表了看法。

sentences.en: They published a paper titled, A Diamond is Forever and Other Fairy Tales.
sentences.zh: 他们发表了一篇题为《钻石恒久远及其他童话故事》的论文。

sentences.en: They looked at how much couples spent on their engagement rings and weddings and tracked how long their marriages lasted.
sentences.zh: 他们研究了情侣在订婚戒指和婚礼上的花费，并追踪了他们的婚姻持续时间。

sentences.en: They found that the more money couples spend on their weddings or engagement rings, the less likely they were to stay together over the long term.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，情侣在婚礼或订婚戒指上花的钱越多，他们长期维持婚姻的可能性就越小。

sentences.en: The opposite was also true.
sentences.zh: 反之亦然。

sentences.en: Spending less on the wedding and engagement ring predicted a longer marriage.
sentences.zh: 在婚礼和订婚戒指上花费较少，预示着婚姻会更长久。

sentences.en: Today, we explore the many ways in which our desire to focus on the beautiful keeps us from attending to the basics.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将探讨我们对美好事物的渴望如何让我们忽略了基本要素的多种方式。

sentences.en: We'll examine how this problem shapes not just individual lives, but organizations and businesses and even public policy.
sentences.zh: 我们将研究这个问题不仅如何影响个人生活，还如何影响组织、企业甚至公共政策。

sentences.en: Why great ideas fail and how to keep them from failing, this week on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 伟大的想法为何会失败，以及如何防止它们失败，本周《隐藏的大脑》为您揭晓。

sentences.en: There's a saying, big dreams start small.
sentences.zh: 有句谚语说，伟大的梦想始于微小。

sentences.en: Bold visions are achieved when we have the tenacity and audacity to pursue them.
sentences.zh: 当我们有毅力和胆量去追求时，大胆的愿景就能实现。

sentences.en: But are great ideas enough to get something off the ground?
sentences.zh: 但伟大的想法足以让事情起步吗？

sentences.en: At Stanford University, Hagi Rao studies this question.
sentences.zh: 在斯坦福大学，哈吉·拉奥研究了这个问题。

sentences.en: He has spent years studying the elements of successful entrepreneurship and innovation.
sentences.zh: 他花了多年时间研究成功创业和创新的要素。

sentences.en: Hagi Rao, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 哈吉·拉奥，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: A pleasure, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你的邀请。

sentences.en: Hagi, I want to start with an example that in recent years has become synonymous with the definition of a public relations disaster, the FIRE Festival.
sentences.zh: 哈吉，我想从近年来成为公关灾难代名词的一个例子开始，那就是火人节（FIRE Festival）。

sentences.en: Let's start at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 让我们从头说起。

sentences.en: In 2016, an American businessman named Billy McFarlane had an app that he was looking to promote.
sentences.zh: 2016年，一位名叫比利·麦克法兰的美国商人有一个他想推广的应用程序。

sentences.en: It was called the FIRE app, F-Y-R-E.
sentences.zh: 它叫FYRE应用，拼写是F-Y-R-E。

sentences.en: What was this app designed to do?
sentences.zh: 这个应用是用来做什么的？

sentences.en: Well, the idea behind the app, Shankar, was to connect artists with clients for performances, appearances, and the like.
sentences.zh: 嗯，尚卡尔，这个应用背后的想法是为表演、出场等活动连接艺人和客户。

sentences.en: Part of what they wanted to do was to have a luxury music festival.
sentences.zh: 他们想做的一部分事情是举办一场豪华音乐节。

sentences.en: And initially, the idea was to sort of promote the app, if you will, for booking musical talent.
sentences.zh: 最初，这个想法可以说是为了推广这个用于预订音乐人才的应用。

sentences.en: But then what happened was the festival itself took on a momentum of its own and swiftly overshadowed the app.
sentences.zh: 但后来，音乐节本身产生了一种势头，迅速盖过了应用的风头。

sentences.en: So, I understand they began selling tickets, and some VIP packages ran to $12,000.
sentences.zh: 我听说他们开始卖票了，有些VIP套餐高达12000美元。

sentences.en: What were ticket buyers being promised for that kind of money?
sentences.zh: 买票的人花这么多钱能得到什么承诺？

sentences.en: Very exotic things, I might add.
sentences.zh: 我得说，是非常异国情调的东西。

sentences.en: They were promised accommodation in geodesic domes that were eco-friendly and presumably modern.
sentences.zh: 他们被承诺住在生态友好且想必很现代的测地线穹顶帐篷里。

sentences.en: And celebrity chefs would provide them meals.
sentences.zh: 而且会有名厨为他们提供餐点。

sentences.en: That was the launch of the app, if you will.
sentences.zh: 这就是该应用的发布会，如果你愿意这么说的话。

sentences.en: So, I understand that this event was going to take place in the Bahamas.
sentences.zh: 我听说这个活动要在巴哈马举行。

sentences.en: And Billy McFarlane had heard rumors that the island on which they were going to host the event was associated with the Colombian drug lord Pablo Escobar.
sentences.zh: 比利·麦克法兰听说有传言说他们要举办活动的岛屿与哥伦比亚毒枭巴勃罗·埃斯科巴有关。

sentences.en: And this becomes part of the marketing, the branding, the hype, right?
sentences.zh: 这成了营销、品牌推广和炒作的一部分，对吧？

sentences.en: Completely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: You know, the moment you say Escobar, I mean, you know, quickly, you know, you get notoriety, you get kind of visibility.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你提到埃斯科巴时，我的意思是，很快你就会获得恶名，获得某种曝光度。

sentences.en: For this one, they released material saying this festival was being organized on Pablo Escobar's private island.
sentences.zh: 这一次，他们发布了宣传材料，称这个音乐节是在巴勃罗·埃斯科巴的私人岛屿上组织的。

sentences.en: You know, the sad reality was it was a remote parking lot north of the Sandals Resort.
sentences.zh: 你知道，可悲的现实是，那只是凉鞋度假村北边的一个偏僻停车场。

sentences.en: Oh, my gosh.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So, the language used to describe this festival, it was called an immersive music festival, two transformative weekends.
sentences.zh: 所以，用来描述这个音乐节的语言，它被称为沉浸式音乐节，两个变革性的周末。

sentences.en: It was supposed to be on the boundaries of the impossible.
sentences.zh: 它本应处于不可能的边缘。

sentences.en: I mean, this was really being pitched to the sky.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这真的是在吹得天花乱坠。

sentences.en: But as the big day started to approach, major musical acts started to pull out.
sentences.zh: 但随着大日子临近，主要的音乐表演开始退出。

sentences.en: Why were they pulling out, Hagi?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么要退出，哈吉？

sentences.en: Well, they had, if you will, aspirations of what this festival ought to be, but they completely overlooked the details.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们对这个音乐节应该是什么样有愿景，但他们完全忽略了细节。

sentences.en: There wasn't enough dirt underneath the fingernails of people who were responsible for making this happen.
sentences.zh: 负责实现这一切的人没有足够的实干经验。

sentences.en: So, they didn't have expertise, they didn't have experience, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，他们没有专业知识，没有经验，你知道，

sentences.en: they were trying to do something within a period of six to eight weeks that takes about 12 months to accomplish.
sentences.zh: 他们试图在六到八周内完成需要大约12个月才能完成的事情。

sentences.en: Billy McFarlane and the other organizers elected to house the guests in tents.
sentences.zh: 比利·麦克法兰和其他组织者选择让客人们住在帐篷里。

sentences.en: The day before the festival was to start, heavy rains lashed the island.
sentences.zh: 音乐节开始的前一天，大雨袭击了该岛。

sentences.en: By then, the first flights were already landing in, people were there, and these initial arrivals were brought to an, I guess,
sentences.zh: 到那时，第一批航班已经降落，人们已经到了那里，这些最初到达的人被带到了一个，我想，

sentences.en: what can be described as an impromptu beach party that lasted for six hours.
sentences.zh: 可以被描述为持续了六个小时的即兴海滩派对的地方。

sentences.en: Basically, they were plied with alcohol and they were just waiting where people were scrambling to build the site.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们被灌了酒，只能在那里等着，而人们正在争先恐后地搭建场地。

sentences.en: I mean, that's just horrifying.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这太可怕了。

sentences.en: At some point now, the people need a place to sleep at night.
sentences.zh: 现在，人们总得有个地方睡觉吧。

sentences.en: What happens?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么？

sentences.en: Were there enough tents for everyone?
sentences.zh: 帐篷够所有人住吗？

sentences.en: Not really.
sentences.zh: 并不够。

sentences.en: I mean, you had scattered disaster relief tents with dirty floors, with soaking wet mattresses and the like.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你看到的是散乱的救灾帐篷，地板很脏，床垫湿透了之类的。

sentences.en: And you can imagine and visualize that late arrivals were being brought to the festival by school bus.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象并描绘出后来到达的人是被校车带到音乐节现场的。

sentences.en: And as soon as they came in, the disarray and the lack of infrastructure was very, very clear to all of the incoming guests.
sentences.zh: 他们一进来，所有的客人都非常清楚这里的混乱和基础设施的匮乏。

sentences.en: The gourmet food, of course, was nothing more than cheese sandwiches served in foam containers.
sentences.zh: 当然，所谓的美味佳肴不过是用泡沫盒装的奶酪三明治。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So apparently there were the problems included a lack of medical personnel on site.
sentences.zh: 所以显然，问题还包括现场缺乏医务人员。

sentences.en: There wasn't running water.
sentences.zh: 没有自来水。

sentences.en: People were told that this was a cash free festival.
sentences.zh: 人们被告知这是一个无现金音乐节。

sentences.en: And so they hadn't brought money to the event and they couldn't even figure out a way to to make alternate arrangements.
sentences.zh: 所以他们没带钱去现场，甚至想不出办法来做其他安排。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, initially, as a matter of fact, I think there were about 500 or so people.
sentences.zh: 你知道，事实上，最初我想大约有500人左右。

sentences.en: They just didn't have enough tents.
sentences.zh: 他们就是没有足够的帐篷。

sentences.en: And you know what they did?
sentences.zh: 你知道他们做了什么吗？

sentences.en: They just stole them from others.
sentences.zh: 他们直接从别人那里偷。

sentences.en: So, and the attendees couldn't even go to the nearby Sandals Resort because it was actually peak season.
sentences.zh: 所以，参加者甚至不能去附近的凉鞋度假村，因为当时正是旺季。

sentences.en: And so, you know, you can imagine people without food, without shelter, without money.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以想象人们没有食物，没有住所，没有钱。

sentences.en: You can imagine what kind of social disintegration quickly ensues.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象随之而来的社会崩溃是什么样的。

sentences.en: So eventually, apparently, only a small number of local musicians ever played at this festival for a few hours.
sentences.zh: 所以最终，显然只有少数当地音乐人在这个音乐节上演奏了几个小时。

sentences.en: And of course, people started to see that things were falling apart.
sentences.zh: 当然，人们开始看到事情正在分崩离析。

sentences.en: They were scrambling to get home.
sentences.zh: 他们争先恐后地想回家。

sentences.en: But even here, it was difficult to get flights back.
sentences.zh: 但即使在这里，也很难买到回程机票。

sentences.en: People were stuck at the airport for hours.
sentences.zh: 人们在机场被困了几个小时。

sentences.en: So even the evacuation turned out to be something of a disaster.
sentences.zh: 所以连撤离过程都变成了一场灾难。

sentences.en: Completely.
sentences.zh: 完全是这样。

sentences.en: First of all, I mean, there was, you know, an onrush of potential passengers to the airport.
sentences.zh: 首先，我的意思是，有大量的潜在乘客涌向机场。

sentences.en: Even that was really delayed.
sentences.zh: 即使是这样也真的被耽误了。

sentences.en: And so you got people essentially in a trap.
sentences.zh: 所以人们基本上被困住了。

sentences.en: What was the aftermath of all of this, Hagi?
sentences.zh: 这一切的后果是什么，哈吉？

sentences.en: What happened to the organizers, Billy McFarland and his colleagues?
sentences.zh: 组织者比利·麦克法兰和他的同事们怎么样了？

sentences.en: Did they face any penalties for doing this?
sentences.zh: 他们因为这样做面临任何惩罚吗？

sentences.en: They certainly did.
sentences.zh: 他们当然面临了。

sentences.en: You know, immediately, there was like a $100 million lawsuit in the state of California.
sentences.zh: 你知道，加利福尼亚州立即就有一项1亿美元的诉讼。

sentences.en: And they wanted class action status.
sentences.zh: 他们想要集体诉讼的地位。

sentences.en: And they had 150 plaintiffs.
sentences.zh: 他们有150名原告。

sentences.en: And it was for breach of contract, covenant, misrepresentation, all of that.
sentences.zh: 诉讼理由包括违约、契约、虚假陈述等等。

sentences.en: And in the end, McFarland was sentenced to six years in prison in 2018.
sentences.zh: 最终，麦克法兰在2018年被判处六年监禁。

sentences.en: And he had to forfeit $26 million.
sentences.zh: 他还必须没收2600万美元。

sentences.en: What went wrong with the Fyre Festival?
sentences.zh: 火人节到底出了什么问题？

sentences.en: A better question might be, what didn't go wrong?
sentences.zh: 一个更好的问题可能是，什么没出问题？

sentences.en: When we come back, how visionaries fail by not taking into account the planning, preparation,
sentences.zh: 当我们回来时，我们将探讨梦想家们如何因为没有考虑到真正的成功所需要的规划、准备、

sentences.en: and precision that is needed for real success.
sentences.zh: 和精确性而失败。

sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: We all have big dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 我们都有伟大的梦想。

sentences.en: Launch a business.
sentences.zh: 创办一家企业。

sentences.en: Get a degree.
sentences.zh: 获得一个学位。

sentences.en: Start a family.
sentences.zh: 组建一个家庭。

sentences.en: What does it take to do those things?
sentences.zh: 做这些事情需要什么？

sentences.en: Passion?
sentences.zh: 激情？

sentences.en: Heart?
sentences.zh: 真心？

sentences.en: Vision?
sentences.zh: 愿景？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: But at Stanford University, Hagi Rao says there are other elements that may matter more.
sentences.zh: 但在斯坦福大学，哈吉·拉奥说还有其他可能更重要的要素。

sentences.en: When we overlook them, we can fail to do the great things we aspire to do.
sentences.zh: 当我们忽略它们时，我们就无法实现我们渴望做到的伟大事情。

sentences.en: Hagi, I want to go back to the year 1987.
sentences.zh: 哈吉，我想回到1987年。

sentences.en: In Pyongyang, North Korea, construction begins on a new hotel.
sentences.zh: 在朝鲜平壤，一家新酒店开始动工。

sentences.en: But it's not any old hotel.
sentences.zh: 但它不是普通的酒店。

sentences.en: It's supposed to outdo a South Korean hotel that was, at the time, the tallest hotel in the world?
sentences.zh: 它本应超过当时世界上最高的酒店——一家韩国酒店？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: This was the Roo Gyeong Hotel, I think also called the capital of the willows, I believe,
sentences.zh: 这就是柳京饭店，我想它也被称为“柳京”，我相信，

sentences.en: given the older name for Pyongyang.
sentences.zh: 考虑到平壤的旧称。

sentences.en: And indeed, it was a response to what the South Koreans were doing with the Olympics.
sentences.zh: 确实，这是对韩国人举办奥运会所作出的回应。

sentences.en: So, they wanted to build a hotel for a socialist version of the Olympics, the World Festival of Youth.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们想为社会主义版本的奥运会——世界青年与学生联欢节建造一家酒店。

sentences.en: And the idea was to build this massive hotel called the Roo Gyeong Hotel.
sentences.zh: 想法就是建造这座名为柳京饭店的巨大酒店。

sentences.en: And to me, Shankar, the rivalry between two nations and two leaders and all of that,
sentences.zh: 对我来说，尚卡尔，两个国家和两位领导人之间的竞争等等，

sentences.en: it really makes me wonder about how leaders can easily be seduced by the edifice complex,
sentences.zh: 这真的让我思考领导者如何容易被“大厦情结”所诱惑，

sentences.en: as opposed to the edifice complex.
sentences.zh: 而不是真正的建设情结。

sentences.en: And this is a stellar example of the edifice complex.
sentences.zh: 这是一个大厦情结的典型例子。

sentences.en: So, the building was to have three wings, each sloped at a 75-degree angle that converged into
sentences.zh: 所以，这座建筑有三个侧翼，每个侧翼以75度角倾斜，汇聚成

sentences.en: what looked like a pyramid, 3,000 rooms, 1,000 feet tall.
sentences.zh: 看起来像金字塔的形状，有3000个房间，1000英尺高。

sentences.en: It was supposed to be an engineering marvel that would demonstrate that North Korea was
sentences.zh: 这本应是一个工程奇迹，旨在证明朝鲜

sentences.en: superior to South Korea.
sentences.zh: 优于韩国。

sentences.en: The only thing was the North Koreans didn't have expertise and experience with a variety of
sentences.zh: 唯一的问题是，朝鲜人缺乏各种

sentences.en: building materials.
sentences.zh: 建筑材料方面的专业知识和经验。

sentences.en: So, typically, they built things with concrete.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们通常用混凝土来建造。

sentences.en: And to gain that 1,000 feet height and all of that, you truly had to have an enormous base.
sentences.zh: 为了达到那1000英尺的高度以及所有这些要求，你确实需要一个巨大的地基。

sentences.en: And that kind of made it for an even larger kind of footprint, if you will.
sentences.zh: 可以说，这导致了更大的占地面积。

sentences.en: So, almost right from the beginning, the construction project runs into probleMs.
sentences.zh: 所以，几乎从一开始，这个建设项目就遇到了问题。

sentences.en: It was to be built in time for this major sporting event.
sentences.zh: 它本应赶在这个大型体育赛事之前建成。

sentences.en: But I understand it wasn't ready by the time the sporting event rolls around?
sentences.zh: 但我听说在体育赛事开始时它还没准备好？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: In fact, it wasn't because of a variety of engineering issues.
sentences.zh: 事实上，确实是因为各种工程问题。

sentences.en: Even though the government had spent, you know, I assume billions of dollars,
sentences.zh: 尽管政府已经投入了，你知道，我想是数十亿美元，

sentences.en: they'd also improved the airport.
sentences.zh: 他们还改善了机场。

sentences.en: They'd kind of improved roads and everything.
sentences.zh: 他们改善了道路以及其他一切设施。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, at around this time, the Soviet Union was actually disintegrating.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，大约在这个时候，苏联实际上正在解体。

sentences.en: And aid and investment that the North Koreans were accustomed to from the Soviet Union,
sentences.zh: 朝鲜人习惯从苏联获得的援助和投资，

sentences.en: they actually kind of dwindled to a trickle.
sentences.zh: 实际上已经缩减到了涓涓细流。

sentences.en: And, you know, and North Korea was headed for an economic crisis.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，朝鲜正面临经济危机。

sentences.en: So, it was this economic crisis that kind of led to the abandonment of this project.
sentences.zh: 所以，正是这场经济危机导致了这个项目的废弃。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: So, in 1992, this is five years after construction begins,
sentences.zh: 所以，在1992年，也就是开工五年后，

sentences.en: the project is halted.
sentences.zh: 项目停工了。

sentences.en: And, in fact, a crane is abandoned on top of the building.
sentences.zh: 事实上，一台起重机被遗弃在了大楼顶部。

sentences.en: It must now look like a very strange pyramid.
sentences.zh: 它现在看起来一定像一座非常奇怪的金字塔。

sentences.en: And the building just simply sits there.
sentences.zh: 大楼就那样矗立在那里。

sentences.en: It sits unoccupied, vacant for decades.
sentences.zh: 它空置了数十年，无人问津。

sentences.en: That's exactly right, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 完全正确，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: But by then, you know, you already had memes describing this hotel as the Hotel of Doom
sentences.zh: 但到那时，你知道，已经有模因把这家酒店称为“末日酒店”

sentences.en: or the Tower of Failure and, you know, so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 或者“失败之塔”，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And what this was, was really an architectural testament to the excesses of the Pyongyang regime.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是平壤政权过度行为的建筑见证。

sentences.en: So, this massive structure sits today.
sentences.zh: 所以，这座巨大的建筑今天依然矗立着。

sentences.en: It's basically a ghost hotel.
sentences.zh: 它基本上是一座鬼酒店。

sentences.en: It must look eerie, Huggy.
sentences.zh: 它看起来一定很阴森，哈吉。

sentences.en: It truly is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Because the problem is the building was structurally unsound.
sentences.zh: 因为问题在于这座建筑在结构上是不稳固的。

sentences.en: Even though from the exterior, the building may look sound, the interior is the problem.
sentences.zh: 尽管从外观上看，这座建筑可能看起来很稳固，但内部才是问题所在。

sentences.en: And because it was built with concrete, it would take an enormous amount of time and expense
sentences.zh: 而且因为它是由混凝土建造的，需要花费大量的时间和金钱

sentences.en: to redo the ventilation systems and, you know, the air conditioning systems,
sentences.zh: 来重做通风系统，你知道，还有空调系统，

sentences.en: all of which were created for 1980s specification.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都是按照20世纪80年代的规格建造的。

sentences.en: So, you say that the Fyre Festival and this Hotel of Doom are examples of what researchers call
sentences.zh: 所以，你说“火人节”和这个“末日酒店”是研究人员所称的

sentences.en: poetry before plumbing.
sentences.zh: “诗意先于管道”的例子。

sentences.en: Unpack the term for me, Huggy.
sentences.zh: 为我解读一下这个术语，哈吉。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: You know, I should immediately give credit to my wonderful colleague,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我应该立即向我出色的同事致敬，

sentences.en: who sadly passed away several years ago, Jim March.
sentences.zh: 他几年前不幸去世了，吉姆·马奇。

sentences.en: He wrote a brilliant book.
sentences.zh: 他写了一本精彩的书。

sentences.en: And that's kind of where he said, hey, leadership is a mix of poetry and plumbing.
sentences.zh: 他在书中提到，嘿，领导力是诗意与管道的结合。

sentences.en: And he used poetry as a shorthand for purpose, if you will.
sentences.zh: 他用“诗意”作为目的的速记，如果你愿意的话。

sentences.en: Lofty goals, lofty visions and the like.
sentences.zh: 崇高的目标、崇高的愿景等等。

sentences.en: And plumbing for operational details, efficiency, routines and the like.
sentences.zh: 而“管道”则代表运营细节、效率、常规等等。

sentences.en: And for him, you know, it was, how shall I put it?
sentences.zh: 对他来说，你知道，该怎么说呢？

sentences.en: He saw this as part of like a perennial duality of leadership.
sentences.zh: 他认为这是领导力永恒二元性的一部分。

sentences.en: The exuberant part of a leader's job, the poetry and the purpose, and the prosaic part of the job.
sentences.zh: 领导者工作中充满活力的一部分，即诗意和目的，以及工作中平淡的一部分。

sentences.en: And the prosaic part of the job had to do with simplicity, detail, and kind of making sure things kind of got done.
sentences.zh: 而工作中平淡的部分与简单、细节以及确保事情完成有关。

sentences.en: And what the Fyre Festival and the Hotel of Doom are compelling examples of is how if we get seduced only by the poetry
sentences.zh: “火人节”和“末日酒店”之所以是令人信服的例子，是因为如果我们只被诗意所诱惑

sentences.en: and we forget the plumbing, we are going to be in the grip of, frankly, an illusion.
sentences.zh: 而忘记了管道，坦率地说，我们将陷入一种幻觉之中。

sentences.en: Poetry can be really sometimes a doorway to disaster.
sentences.zh: 诗意有时真的可能是通往灾难的大门。

sentences.en: Hagi, I'm wondering, are there personal dimensions of this as well?
sentences.zh: 哈吉，我想知道，这是否也有个人层面的因素？

sentences.en: Are there times in our personal lives when we can get caught up by the vision, by the poetry, by the passion of something
sentences.zh: 在我们的个人生活中，是否也有时候会被某种愿景、诗意、激情所吸引，

sentences.en: and forget about the prosaic, the mundane, the details?
sentences.zh: 而忘记了平淡、平凡和细节？

sentences.en: Easy to do that.
sentences.zh: 这很容易做到。

sentences.en: Very easy to do that.
sentences.zh: 非常容易做到。

sentences.en: And very easy to stumble into a disaster.
sentences.zh: 而且很容易陷入灾难。

sentences.en: I prefer to think of the poet and the plumber as two selves that all of us have.
sentences.zh: 我更倾向于把诗人与管道工看作我们每个人都拥有的两个自我。

sentences.en: And so what we've got to kind of ask ourselves is, which self is actually showing up?
sentences.zh: 所以我们必须问自己的是，到底是哪一个自我出现了？

sentences.en: At home, if it's all plumbing and no poetry, my God, there's no laughter, there's no conversation, it's kind of boring.
sentences.zh: 在家里，如果全是管道而没有诗意，天哪，没有欢笑，没有对话，那太无聊了。

sentences.en: But at the same token, if it's all poetry and no plumbing, you know, who's going to fix the lights and who's going to fix the water system?
sentences.zh: 但同样，如果全是诗意而没有管道，你知道，谁来修理灯具，谁来修理供水系统？

sentences.en: You know, all of those things.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所有这些事情。

sentences.en: You're going to run into difficulty.
sentences.zh: 你会遇到困难。

sentences.en: So in that sense, our life is a perennial effort to kind of balance and toggle between our plumber selves and our poet selves.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个意义上说，我们的生活是一种在管道工自我和诗人自我之间不断平衡和切换的努力。

sentences.en: Can you talk a little bit about this idea in an organizational setting where we can get very enamored with the pleasure of brainstorming an idea or brainstorming a new startup
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈在组织环境中，我们如何容易沉迷于头脑风暴一个想法或初创企业的乐趣，

sentences.en: instead of thinking about the nitty-gritty, the details that go into actually launching the startup?
sentences.zh: 而不是去思考启动初创企业所需的具体细节吗？

sentences.en: Completely.
sentences.zh: 完全同意。

sentences.en: You immediately fall prey to a bias called the addition bias.
sentences.zh: 你会立即成为一种被称为“加法偏见”的受害者。

sentences.en: So very quickly, you add things for people to do.
sentences.zh: 所以很快，你就会增加人们需要做的事情。

sentences.en: They're already overwhelmed because of time poverty.
sentences.zh: 他们已经因为时间匮乏而不知所措了。

sentences.en: I mean, where are they going to find the resources to do all of this?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们去哪里寻找资源来完成所有这些工作？

sentences.en: So very little actually gets done.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上很少有事情能真正完成。

sentences.en: I feel like everyone is familiar with the brainstorming session at a company where, you know, everyone puts up sticky notes on a wall saying,
sentences.zh: 我觉得每个人都熟悉公司的头脑风暴会议，你知道，每个人都在墙上贴上便签，说，

sentences.en: here are the ideas that we should do.
sentences.zh: 这是我们应该做的想法。

sentences.en: And there is something deeply pleasurable in doing that and thinking about blue sky ideas of ways that you can change and things that you can transform.
sentences.zh: 这样做确实有一种深深的快感，去思考改变和转型的蓝天构想。

sentences.en: But that is a far cry from actually making those transformations real.
sentences.zh: 但这与真正实现这些转型相去甚远。

sentences.en: I love your description of the brainstorming experience, Shankar, because when people think of what brainstorming is,
sentences.zh: 尚卡尔，我喜欢你对头脑风暴体验的描述，因为当人们想到什么是头脑风暴时，

sentences.en: it's kind of putting fun ideas and often implausible ideas on the table.
sentences.zh: 它往往是把有趣的、通常是不可行的想法摆在桌面上。

sentences.en: But brainstorming without constraints is a problem.
sentences.zh: 但是没有约束的头脑风暴是一个问题。

sentences.en: How can you brainstorm without talking to a customer?
sentences.zh: 你怎么能在不与客户交谈的情况下进行头脑风暴呢？

sentences.en: You suggested the launch some years ago of the healthcare.gov system illustrates this idea.
sentences.zh: 你曾提到几年前healthcare.gov系统的推出说明了这个想法。

sentences.en: Tell me what happened there, Hagi.
sentences.zh: 告诉我那里发生了什么，哈吉。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: You know, this was after President Obama signed the Affordable Care Act.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是在奥巴马总统签署《平价医疗法案》之后。

sentences.en: And then there was a website that was to be launched, and it was called healthcare.gov.
sentences.zh: 然后有一个网站要推出，叫healthcare.gov。

sentences.en: The hope was that the platform would, you know, enroll lots of uninsured Americans.
sentences.zh: 希望该平台能让许多未参保的美国人注册。

sentences.en: But the rollout was an exercise in complete disaster.
sentences.zh: 但这次发布是一场彻底的灾难。

sentences.en: As a matter of fact, on the first day that healthcare.gov was launched, 4 million unique visitors visited the portal,
sentences.zh: 事实上，在healthcare.gov推出的第一天，有400万独立访客访问了该门户网站，

sentences.en: but only six were able to successfully register themselves.
sentences.zh: 但只有六个人成功注册。

sentences.en: Can you imagine that?
sentences.zh: 你能想象吗？

sentences.en: You know, and then over the next few days, their site had 8 million visitors,
sentences.zh: 你知道，在接下来的几天里，他们的网站有800万访客，

sentences.en: but only 1% enrolled in that healthcare plan.
sentences.zh: 但只有1%的人注册了该医疗计划。

sentences.en: And even those who enrolled encountered lots of errors and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 即使是那些注册的人也遇到了很多错误，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Because, you know, it's like healthcare.gov was not a simple app.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，healthcare.gov并不是一个简单的应用程序。

sentences.en: It was very complicated because it needed to integrate data from different sources.
sentences.zh: 它非常复杂，因为它需要整合来自不同来源的数据。

sentences.en: You needed data on social security numbers, data on income, and then you needed what the states were doing and all of that
sentences.zh: 你需要社会安全号码数据、收入数据，然后你需要各州在做什么，以及所有这些，

sentences.en: before matching people with private purveyors of insurance.
sentences.zh: 在将人们与私人保险供应商匹配之前。

sentences.en: You had to have ID verification.
sentences.zh: 你必须进行身份验证。

sentences.en: All of this is, like, pretty complex.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都相当复杂。

sentences.en: And it's not just putting, like, an app out there.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是发布一个应用程序。

sentences.en: And that was why it actually ballooned into this tragic disaster.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么它最终演变成这场悲剧性的灾难。

sentences.en: But subsequently, you know, it must be mentioned, there was remarkable recovery.
sentences.zh: 但随后，你知道，必须提到的是，出现了显著的恢复。

sentences.en: The CTO of the Obama presidency, Todd Park, I think they changed the leadership.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马总统任期的首席技术官托德·帕克，我想他们更换了领导层。

sentences.en: They fired a bunch of people.
sentences.zh: 他们解雇了一群人。

sentences.en: So lots of other things happened in order to retrieve ground.
sentences.zh: 所以为了挽回局面，发生了很多其他事情。

sentences.en: And eventually, it did kind of do better, much better.
sentences.zh: 最终，它确实做得更好，好多了。

sentences.en: So you and your colleague, Bob Sutton, who is a former Hidden Brain guest,
sentences.zh: 所以你和你的同事鲍勃·萨顿，他是Hidden Brain的前嘉宾，

sentences.en: you both say that another reason we tend to prioritize poetry over plumbing
sentences.zh: 你们都说我们倾向于优先考虑诗意而非管道的另一个原因是，

sentences.en: is that the feedback mechanisms are broken and problems are not being reported to leaders.
sentences.zh: 反馈机制被破坏了，问题没有上报给领导者。

sentences.en: So people become silent, and it creates the illusion that everything is working well.
sentences.zh: 所以人们变得沉默，这造成了一切运作良好的错觉。

sentences.en: The reason you have illusion is 30 years of research shows us
sentences.zh: 之所以会有错觉，是因为30年的研究向我们表明，

sentences.en: that people who are powerful and who feel they have power,
sentences.zh: 那些有权势且感到自己有权势的人，

sentences.en: they actually don't search much.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上并不怎么去探究。

sentences.en: It's people without power that search and figure out why are things happening the way they are.
sentences.zh: 是那些没有权力的人在探究并弄清楚事情为什么会这样发生。

sentences.en: The other thing is, to your point,
sentences.zh: 另一件事是，正如你所说，

sentences.en: not only is there silence,
sentences.zh: 不仅存在沉默，

sentences.en: people in power have an army of people making their life easy.
sentences.zh: 掌权者有一群人让他们的生活变得轻松。

sentences.en: So they also don't know how jobs three levels beneath them are done.
sentences.zh: 所以他们也不知道他们下属三级的工作是如何完成的。

sentences.en: So illusion hardens into impatience.
sentences.zh: 因此，幻觉固化为不耐烦。

sentences.en: Why couldn't we get it done yesterday and so on?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们昨天不能完成它，等等？

sentences.en: And the moment you multiply illusion with impatience,
sentences.zh: 当你把幻觉与不耐烦相乘的那一刻，

sentences.en: what happens is the really competent doers,
sentences.zh: 发生的事情是，真正能干的实干家，

sentences.en: they go underground.
sentences.zh: 他们转入地下了。

sentences.en: Because they know this is a fast train right to nowhere.
sentences.zh: 因为他们知道这是一列通往虚无的快车。

sentences.en: So you have incompetent people who are available to help you proceed with whatever you're doing.
sentences.zh: 所以你剩下的是那些愿意帮助你进行任何事情的无能之辈。

sentences.en: And now you have incompetence, multiplying, impatience, and delusion.
sentences.zh: 现在你有了无能，加上不耐烦和妄想。

sentences.en: So even when you tell people up the hierarchy something wrong is happening,
sentences.zh: 所以即使你告诉层级上方的人出了问题，

sentences.en: it's very difficult for them to register because they don't understand it.
sentences.zh: 他们也很难理解，因为他们根本不懂。

sentences.en: The canonical stories about the American automobile industry and the executives there,
sentences.zh: 关于美国汽车工业和那里的高管的经典故事是，

sentences.en: any time they had a car with a problem,
sentences.zh: 每当他们的车出现问题时，

sentences.en: they never had to go to the mechanic.
sentences.zh: 他们从来不需要去修理厂。

sentences.en: I mean, it was immediately replaced.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它会被立即更换。

sentences.en: So you've no idea what it means for a person to go to the mechanic.
sentences.zh: 所以你根本不知道一个人去修理厂意味着什么。

sentences.en: And so you can actually see the disconnection
sentences.zh: 因此，你实际上可以看到这种脱节，

sentences.en: that immediately kind of derails a lot of these plans and projects and so on.
sentences.zh: 它立即破坏了许多这些计划和项目等等。

sentences.en: Another reason we don't do enough plumbing is that we don't increase the amount of plumbing
sentences.zh: 我们没有做足够管道工作的另一个原因是，随着我们从最初的愿景中成长和扩张，

sentences.en: we will need as we grow and expand from our initial visions.
sentences.zh: 我们没有增加所需的管道工作量。

sentences.en: Talk about the challenge of scaling, Hagi, and how that presents a problem for plumbing.
sentences.zh: 谈谈规模化的挑战，哈吉，以及它如何给管道工作带来问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, scaling for me is reinvention.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对我来说，规模化就是重塑。

sentences.en: The simplest way in which I can telegraph this is Bob and I wrote a case study
sentences.zh: 我能传达这一点的最简单方式是，鲍勃和我写了一个案例研究，

sentences.en: about the former CTO of Uber.
sentences.zh: 关于Uber的前首席技术官。

sentences.en: And we asked him a simple question.
sentences.zh: 我们问了他一个简单的问题。

sentences.en: He said, hey, how long have you worked at Uber?
sentences.zh: 我说，嘿，你在优步工作多久了？

sentences.en: And he looks at us and said, four years.
sentences.zh: 他看着我们说，四年了。

sentences.en: But it feels as though I work for 16 different companies.
sentences.zh: 但感觉就像我在16家不同的公司工作过一样。

sentences.en: And what does he mean by that?
sentences.zh: 他这话是什么意思呢？

sentences.en: Four years?
sentences.zh: 四年？

sentences.en: How can you feel like you're working for 16 different companies?
sentences.zh: 你怎么会感觉自己在16家不同的公司工作？

sentences.en: And the answer is every quarter Uber is a different company.
sentences.zh: 答案是，优步每个季度都是一家不同的公司。

sentences.en: And the problem is changing the plumbing involves two things.

sentences.en: Can you imagine your Ridgeway?
sentences.zh: 你能想象李奇微当时的处境吗？

sentences.en: I mean, you've got like thousands of demotivated, demoralized, tired troops.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你有成千上万士气低落、疲惫不堪的部队。

sentences.zh: 你不能向你的老板

sentences.en: for more fresh troops from the US.

sentences.en: That'll take six months to come there.

sentences.zh: 到那时，一切都已成定局。

sentences.en: And the marvel behind what Ridgway did was, the same overwhelmed, demoralized group of people,
sentences.zh: 而李奇微所做之事的奇迹在于，同样这群不知所措、士气低落的人，

sentences.en: Ridgway actually got them to move and push the Chinese and the others.
sentences.zh: 李奇微竟然让他们动了起来，并击退了中国军队和其他人。

sentences.en: And how did he do it?
sentences.zh: 他是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: You know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，

sentences.en: there are lots of things he did.
sentences.zh: 他做了很多事情。

sentences.en: I just want to give our, you know, listeners a couple of things
sentences.zh: 我只想给我们的听众讲讲他做的

sentences.en: he did.
sentences.zh: 几件事。

sentences.en: One of the very first things Ridgway realizes is, you know, I've never fought in Korea.
sentences.zh: 李奇微意识到的第一件事就是，你知道，我从未在韩国打过仗。

sentences.en: I don't even know how the land looks like.

sentences.en: Where are mountains?

sentences.en: Where are rivers?

sentences.en: Where are lakes?
sentences.zh: 湖在哪里？

sentences.en: So, he actually persuades a bomber pilot to take him on as a navigator and says, I'll help you

sentences.en: navigate.

sentences.en: I just want to see what's ahead.

sentences.en: And you know, there he is.

sentences.en: oh my God, there's this complicated landscape.

sentences.zh: 你知道，我不知道，或者我不知道那里有一条需要跨越的河流，或者

sentences.zh: 所以他的吉普车后面总是

sentences.en: In other words, they don't get so caught up in the poetry that they forget about the plumbing.

sentences.en: There's a narrative that we hear over and over again in news reporting and on social media.
sentences.zh: 我们在新闻报道和社交媒体上反复听到一种叙事。

sentences.en: People are more divided than ever, by class, by education, and especially by political beliefs.
sentences.zh: 人们比以往任何时候都更加分裂，按阶级、教育程度，尤其是政治信仰。

sentences.en: We see evidence for this narrative in lots of places.
sentences.zh: 我们在很多地方都能看到这种叙事的证据。

sentences.en: People ignore those who disagree with them
sentences.zh: 人们往往会忽视那些与自己意见相左的人，

sentences.en: or gaze upon their political opponents with a mixture of bewilderment, contempt, and anger.
sentences.zh: 或者带着困惑、蔑视和愤怒的复杂情绪审视自己的政治对手。

sentences.en: What we hear less often are ideas for how to change this narrative.
sentences.zh: 但我们很少听到关于如何改变这种叙事方式的建议。

sentences.en: Is it possible to actually find common ground with someone whose worldview is the polar opposite of your own?
sentences.zh: 我们真的有可能与一个世界观与自己截然相反的人找到共同点吗？

sentences.en: How can we actually persuade someone else of our point of view?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何真正说服别人接受我们的观点？

sentences.en: What would it take for us to be persuaded by theirs?
sentences.zh: 我们需要什么条件才会被对方说服？

sentences.en: We pondered these questions some time ago with Rob Willer.
sentences.zh: 前段时间，我们和罗伯·威勒（Rob Willer）一起思考了这些问题。

sentences.en: He's a sociologist at Stanford University,
sentences.zh: 他是斯坦福大学的一位社会学家，

sentences.en: and he joined us for an episode titled, Win Hearts, Then Mines.
sentences.zh: 他曾参加过我们一期名为《先赢人心，再论是非》的节目。

sentences.en: Today, he returns to the show to answer
sentences.zh: 今天，他再次做客节目，

sentences.en: listener questions about engaging with people who are different from us.
sentences.zh: 回答听众关于如何与不同立场的人进行交流的问题。

sentences.en: Rob Willer, welcome back to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 罗伯·威勒，欢迎回到《隐藏的大脑》（Hidden Brain）。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请。

sentences.en: Rob, in our earlier conversation, we talked about how when you were a kid, you moved from Kansas to South Carolina.
sentences.zh: 罗伯，在我们之前的谈话中，你提到小时候从堪萨斯州搬到了南卡罗来纳州。

sentences.en: The community you moved to was, politically speaking, very different from the one you'd left,
sentences.zh: 从政治角度来看，你搬去的那个社区与你离开的地方非常不同，

sentences.en: and it was something of a culture shock.
sentences.zh: 这让你经历了一场文化冲击。

sentences.en: What were some of the things that stood out to you when you first arrived in South Carolina?
sentences.zh: 当你刚到南卡罗来纳州时，有哪些事情让你印象深刻？

sentences.en: Well, when I moved from Kansas to South Carolina, a key thing was that I was moving from this small college town, Lawrence, Kansas,
sentences.zh: 嗯，当我从堪萨斯州搬到南卡罗来纳州时，关键的一点是我从堪萨斯州劳伦斯市那个小大学城搬出来的，

sentences.en: that was very politically, culturally progressive, not that religious, you know, fairly secular.
sentences.zh: 那里在政治和文化上非常进步，宗教色彩不浓，你知道，相当世俗化。

sentences.en: And I moved to South Carolina in 1988, and found myself in just a very different political, cultural environment.
sentences.zh: 1988年我搬到南卡罗来纳州，发现自己置身于一个政治和文化环境截然不同的地方。

sentences.en: And a place that was characterized as much as anything by deep scars from racial segregation, Jim Crow, and even the Civil War.
sentences.zh: 那个地方最显著的特征之一，就是种族隔离、吉姆·克劳法甚至内战留下的深刻伤痕。

sentences.en: Even the wounds of the Civil War were still healing on the surface.
sentences.zh: 甚至内战的创伤在表面上都还没有完全愈合。

sentences.en: And it was, for me, just really striking to start to be interacting every day with people who might have racial prejudices,
sentences.zh: 对我来说，每天都要与可能有种族偏见的人打交道，这真的很令人震惊，

sentences.en: hearing the N-word on the playground.
sentences.zh: 在操场上听到针对黑人的歧视性称呼。

sentences.en: It just was really, really shocking.
sentences.zh: 这真的、真的太让人震惊了。

sentences.en: And also just the degree of racial segregation that just happened spontaneously, even amongst 10, 11, 12-year-old kids.
sentences.zh: 而且，即使是在10岁、11岁、12岁的孩子之间，那种自发形成的种族隔离程度也令人吃惊。

sentences.en: People were getting signals about who was supposed to interact with whom, and they were following them.
sentences.zh: 人们接收到关于“应该和谁交往”的信号，并且都在照做。

sentences.en: Our teachers had, you know, at least half of them had taught in racially segregated schools, schools that integrated less than 20 years earlier.
sentences.zh: 我们的老师中，至少有一半曾在种族隔离学校教过书，那些学校在不到20年前才实现种族融合。

sentences.en: All the kids I was going to school with, basically their parents had gone to all black or all white schools.
sentences.zh: 和我一起上学的所有孩子，他们的父母基本上都上过全黑人或全白人的学校。

sentences.en: And so it was really striking to me, coming from a progressive community, where the kind of moral battle of the 60s around civil rights was fairly settled.
sentences.zh: 所以这对我来说真的很震撼，因为我来自一个进步的社区，在那里，60年代关于民权的道德之争已经基本尘埃落定。

sentences.en: And if you expressed racial prejudice in public, you were a moral or social pariah in that community.
sentences.zh: 如果你在公共场合表达种族偏见，你会被那个社区视为道德或社会上的弃儿。

sentences.en: And it just wasn't the same way in the place I'd moved to.
sentences.zh: 但我搬到的那个地方情况却并非如此。

sentences.en: Did you find yourself getting into arguments with people, Rob?
sentences.zh: 罗伯，你当时会和别人争论吗？

sentences.en: I did, yeah.
sentences.zh: 会的，确实会。

sentences.en: As much as anything about race and religion, you know, the things that we had the starkest differences on,
sentences.zh: 除了种族和宗教这些我们分歧最严重的问题外，

sentences.en: there were also, and still are, deeply held beliefs that I would encounter about how the poor were responsible for their own fate
sentences.zh: 我还遇到过一些根深蒂固的观念，比如认为穷人要为自己的命运负责，

sentences.en: and didn't deserve sympathy, and just a lot of cultural beliefs that were very new to me, and for me, very objectionable.
sentences.zh: 不值得同情，还有很多对我来说非常新奇、也非常令人反感的文化观念。

sentences.en: And my first reaction on this was to debate.
sentences.zh: 我最初的反应就是辩论。

sentences.en: You know, I've been raised in this very intellectual household, and I came right back at a lot of these views
sentences.zh: 你知道，我是在一个非常注重知识的家庭长大的，我直接反驳了许多这类观点，

sentences.en: to the extent that I could without becoming like an outcast in my community.
sentences.zh: 在不至于让自己在社区里被孤立的限度内，我尽可能地去反驳。

sentences.en: And that was a really intense and rich experience, because I didn't find I was changing a lot of folks' minds.
sentences.zh: 那是一段非常强烈且丰富的经历，因为我发现自己并没有改变多少人的想法。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So I think many of us approach disagreements and disputes the way you did, as if they're a debate that we can either win or lose.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们很多人处理分歧和争论的方式和你一样，仿佛这是一场非赢即输的辩论。

sentences.en: And so we believe that if we can just present our case clearly and have the best argument and the clearest facts,
sentences.zh: 因此我们相信，只要能清晰地陈述观点，拿出最好的论据和最明确的事实，

sentences.en: we're going to persuade the other person of our point of view.
sentences.zh: 我们就能说服对方接受我们的观点。

sentences.en: You've learned over the years, not just when you moved to South Carolina,
sentences.zh: 多年来你已经了解到，不仅仅是在搬到南卡罗来纳州时，

sentences.en: but later on when you became a researcher, that this does not tend to work.
sentences.zh: 后来当你成为研究人员时也发现，这种方法往往行不通。

sentences.en: Why not, Rob?
sentences.zh: 为什么呢，罗伯？

sentences.en: Well, for one, just coming right back at somebody with another set of facts and an alternate way to reason about some issue
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，直接用另一套事实和另一种推理方式去反驳别人，

sentences.en: is a recipe for competition, for making somebody mad and defensive in the face of your arguments.
sentences.zh: 只会引发竞争，让对方在你的论点面前感到愤怒和防御。

sentences.en: And that might play in a high school debate round where there's a judge who's paying attention to the quality of the arguments.
sentences.zh: 这在高中辩论赛中或许管用，因为有评委在关注论点的质量。

sentences.en: And I was a high school debater and, you know, refined those skills, if you'll call them that,
sentences.zh: 我曾经也是一名高中辩手，你知道，在多年的周末辩论赛中，

sentences.en: in debate tournaments weekend after weekend for years.
sentences.zh: 磨练了那些技巧，如果那也算技巧的话。

sentences.en: But that's not really, as it turns out, a great way to change a person's mind.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，这并不是改变一个人想法的好方法。

sentences.en: It just puts them off generally and maybe makes them mad, could even entrench their views.
sentences.zh: 它通常只会让对方反感，甚至可能让他们愤怒，甚至加深他们的偏见。

sentences.en: And for me, the more helpful experience in terms of learning something about persuasion
sentences.zh: 对我来说，在学习说服技巧方面，

sentences.en: and how it can really work in the real world was my experience working as a union organizer.
sentences.zh: 以及了解它如何在现实世界中真正发挥作用，更有帮助的经历是我做工会组织者的那段时光。

sentences.en: So in graduate school, I went to graduate school at Cornell University
sentences.zh: 我在康奈尔大学读研究生时，

sentences.en: and was very involved in a union organizing drive for graduate students there.
sentences.zh: 非常积极地参与了那里研究生的工会组织工作。

sentences.en: And I got exposed to what I think of as the dominant culture of organizing in the U.S.
